subject: general
question: In India, statutory liquidity ratio is fixed by ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** (RBI) is responsible for fixing the statutory liquidity ratio (SLR) in India.
 
• SLR is a requirement that mandates commercial banks to maintain a certain percentage of their net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) in the form of liquid assets such as cash, gold, or government-approved securities.
 
• The primary objective of SLR is to ensure the solvency of banks and control the expansion of credit.
 
• By adjusting the SLR, the RBI can influence the liquidity and credit growth in the banking system.
 
• SLR is one of the monetary policy tools used by the RBI to manage inflation and ensure financial stability in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** was established on **1st April 1935** and nationalized on **1st January 1949**.
 
• The RBI plays a crucial role in the development strategy of the Government of India.
 
• It regulates the issue and supply of the Indian rupee and oversees the country's main payment systems.
 
• The RBI also manages the country's foreign exchange and monetary policy.
 
• In addition to SLR, the RBI uses various other tools like the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), Repo Rate, and Reverse Repo Rate to regulate the money supply and maintain economic stability.
